justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base-model design was identified that preserves the old BackboneElement inheritance while also making modifier-capable reusable datatypes part of the new DataType/BackboneType branch.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping or aliasing BackboneElement would reduce generated-API churn but would retain the ambiguous datatype hierarchy; generated compatibility aliases are migration mitigations, not base-model alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: the local definitions show `BackboneElement` still means elements inside resources, while R6 adds `DataType` and `BackboneType` so the few modifier-capable reusable datatypes can sit under a datatype branch. The break is mainly generated API, reflection, and StructureDefinition-conversion compatibility rather than old-valid/new-invalid instance content. Because FHIR StructureDefinition inheritance has a single formal `baseDefinition`, R6 could not both preserve the old `BackboneElement` ancestry for those datatypes and make them true `DataType`/`BackboneType` descendants. Without official change notes the rationale is inferred, so the calibrated verdict is `Probably justified` rather than fully `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The tempting less-disruptive designs are to leave the affected datatypes based on `BackboneElement`, or to make `BackboneType` a subtype or alias of `BackboneElement`. Those would preserve old `instanceof`, generated-base-class, and metadata-dispatch behavior, but they would fail the central R6 model goal: the datatype-side artifacts would still not be clean descendants of `DataType`, and the resource-backbone-versus-datatype distinction would remain blurred. A generated compatibility interface, alias, or converter mapping can still be useful migration support, but it is outside the normative base R6 StructureDefinition hierarchy and should not be counted as a backward-compatible base-design alternative.
